_note: printed_value is the claim under audit, not an input to the audit. It is here so a disagreement can be located, and it is the only place our numbers appear.
reference_column_disclosure: The conventional structure-agreement readout on this corpus is scored against the column RNet_structure of OpenKnotBench_data.v4.5.1.csv. That column is the NEURAL PREDICTOR'S OWN PREDICTED STRUCTURE. The file contains no probing-derived structure column. This is disclosed because it makes one claim's comparator another claim's subject, and an auditor who does not know it will mis-scope both.

claims.section: Results / the conventional readout on this corpus
claims.estimand: Two contrasts on the SAME molecules and the SAME strata, each standardised by its own within-stratum standard deviation: (a) the interventional contrast, the matched stratified difference in mean rescue factor between G-C-target and A-U-target interventions; (b) the conventional contrast, the same matched stratified difference computed on a structure-agreement column. Claim: (a) is larger than (b) after standardisation, and (b) additionally moves by a factor when the set of admitted pairs is changed in a defensible way.
claims.what_would_falsify_it: the two contrasts are not on the same weights/strata; or the agreement column is not what the paper says it is; or the standardisation is not by within-stratum SD
independent_route_SPECIFICATION_NOT_IMPL: From OK7a_M2R_data.v4.5.1.csv alone, rebuild the admitted set with the criterion in criterion.md, then compute the matched stratified difference in means with weight w_s = min(n_A(s), n_B(s)) over strata s = (design cell, min(depth,3), crossing).
From OpenKnotBench_data.v4.5.1.csv, take the agreement column the paper names in claims.json:reference_column_disclosure and repeat on identical weights and strata.

Standardise each by the pooled within-stratum SD of ITS OWN outcome column before comparing magnitudes. Comparing the raw contrasts is the error this claim exists to correct; a recomputation that compares them raw has not reproduced the claim.

claims.section: Results / what the instrument reads out
claims.estimand: For each of three predictors, the matched stratified difference in the predictor's OWN output for the mutant target pair, between G-C-target and A-U-target interventions, on the same strata as the measured outcome; plus the same difference on the measured rescue factor. Claim: the neural predictor's output separates the two identities, the two nearest-neighbour predictors differ from each other, and the separation decomposes into an architecture axis and a training-data axis whose difference has an interval.
claims.what_would_falsify_it: any pair of predictors is compared without an interval on the DIFFERENCE; or the three predictor columns are not read on the same records; or the 1-based vs 0-based indexing of the two prediction sources is crossed
independent_route_SPECIFICATION_NOT_IMPL: Recompute each predictor's pair probability for the named (i,j) in the mutant sequence from a partition function of your own choosing for the thermodynamic arm; for the neural and learned-parameter arms use the released weights named in artifacts.json.

Take differences of contrasts PAIRED ON THE SAME BOOTSTRAP RESAMPLE, clustering on the 20 puzzles. A recomputation that reports two separate intervals and no interval on their difference has not reproduced the claim.
Indexing is the trap: one prediction source is 0-based and the other is 1-based. A recomputation that gets the identity contrast right but the pairwise differences wrong should check this first.

claims.section: Results / which flips rescue, and the free baseline nobody reports
claims.estimand: Within each design cell of at least 8 admitted interventions, the Spearman rank correlation between a score and the measured rescue factor, averaged across cells weighted by cell size, with a cluster bootstrap over the 20 puzzles. Scores: each predictor's pair probability, and HELIX DEPTH -- an integer read off the declared target structure, requiring no model. Claim: the paired difference (predictor minus depth) has an interval covering zero for every predictor, so no predictor beats the free integer; and three purpose-built mutation-effect scores lose to it with intervals that EXCLUDE zero on the losing side.
claims.what_would_falsify_it: the difference is read as two point estimates rather than as one interval on the difference -- which is the error the paper itself retracts here; or depth is computed from a predicted structure rather than from the declared target; or the bootstrap resamples interventions rather than puzzles
independent_route_SPECIFICATION_NOT_IMPL: Depth of a pair (a,b) in the declared target structure = the number of consecutive nested pairs stacked outside it, capped by the number stacked inside it; formally min(dep, up) where dep counts k with (a-k-1, b+k+1) paired and up counts k with (a+k+1, b-k-1) paired. No model, no folding, no training data.
Compute the difference INSIDE each bootstrap resample and take the interval of the differences. Two separately-resampled intervals do not answer this claim.

The riboSNitch-style scores are: Euclidean distance between the wild-type and mutant base-pair probability matrices; base-pair distance between the two MFE structures; and |dG_ensemble(mut) - dG_ensemble(wt)|. Their declared sign is NEGATIVE (a rescuing flip preserves structure), so negate before ranking.

claims.section: Results / the ledger: who chose the covariate that carries each number
claims.estimand: Eight covariate-choice channels, each priced by a direct contrast in its own units. Claim: five carry the number (one of them against the reported effect), three are empty, and the empty three are leakage, probe chemistry and the folding model's own free energy. Separately: the prices are NOT shares and may not be summed, because a share is a mediated fraction and the estimator for it is withdrawn by this paper.
claims.what_would_falsify_it: any row is priced by a ratio of two contrasts (that is the withdrawn estimator); or the eight rows are presented as a decomposition of one total; or a channel is priced on a scale it does not share with the row above it
independent_route_SPECIFICATION_NOT_IMPL: This claim is structural, not numerical: check that no row's price is a ratio of two contrasts, that the table is never summed, and that each row's number appears in the section it points at with the same value.

The one row that IS a decomposition (C2, placement) must close as an identity: marginal - matched = observed attenuation, and predicted/observed = the mediated fraction. Check both to 1e-4 and report the residual.

claims.section: Results / the leakage audit, in the main text
claims.estimand: Fraction of design cells whose wild-type sequence, inside the design window, reaches >=0.8 identity to an equal-length substring of some sequence in the neural model's training file; and the within-stratum skill slope on the exposed subset against the unexposed one, for the neural model AND for a thermodynamic model that cannot have memorised anything. Claim: exposure is higher than an earlier deposit-based proxy implied, the channel is still empty because the thermodynamic control falls the same way, and EVERY COUNT IS A LOWER BOUND because the training file obtained is a subset of the full corpus.
claims.what_would_falsify_it: any sentence claims a design is absent from the training set rather than not found in the portion obtained; or the exposure scan uses a candidate index that can record 'no candidate' as 'identity zero'; or the thermodynamic control is omitted, in which case a drop on the exposed subset cannot be told from memory
independent_route_SPECIFICATION_NOT_IMPL: Identity of a query window against a training sequence = max over offsets of (matching positions)/(query length), over every training sequence at least as long as the query. Do it exhaustively; do not build a k-mer candidate index, because an index that finds no candidate must not be allowed to return zero.
The control is the whole argument. Compute the same exposed-versus-unexposed slope for a purely thermodynamic predictor. If it falls too, exposure marks difficulty, not memory.

claims.estimand: A calibration that injects a KNOWN mediated fraction into the real mediator and asks how much of the injected range the estimator's reading covers. Claim: the reading covers only a small fraction of the range the truth covers, so the estimator is uninformative here and the quantity is withdrawn.
claims.what_would_falsify_it: the calibration reports a correlation at a single injection level rather than a span across the sweep -- a correlation at one point is an endpoint artefact and the paper says so
independent_route_SPECIFICATION_NOT_IMPL: Sweep the injected fraction f over [0, 0.75]. Report how far the READING moves against how far the TRUTH moves. A correlation coefficient at one f is not the quantity; leave-one-out the endpoint and see whether the sign survives.
